prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1023; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the policyholder reporting a low-speed collision in a parking lot, with the claimant's vehicle reported as the other car involved. Claim file opened and the insured's coverage confirmed, with the driver listed as a household member of the policyholder.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted by the insured, which confirm some details of the scene, including the position of both vehicles. The damage to the claimant's vehicle matches the impact as described, and no earlier damage to that vehicle is known.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who gave the same account of the collision as in the first report. The police report and the statements taken at the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. No independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 4: Claimant reports neck pain following the collision and has been seen by a treating provider. No earlier injury to the same area of the body is known, but it is not yet clear whether this injury came from this crash.

Entry 5: Treatment has followed a usual course and has tapered off as the claimant improved. Nothing in the file suggests the damage or the injury happened before the coverage period began.

Entry 6: Reviewed the file with the treatment records and vehicle estimate on hand. The injury question remains open pending further medical review, while the vehicle damage and coverage points are settled.
